About a week after the shuffle, a search of floors 30 to 45 leads to a settlement of original cat-people, where Alice's group is being held over a dispute about money and a language skill book. The guards identify Feline as a member of the Spirit Tiger tribe. Ken finds Alice, who doubts him because of how he has changed, and Dez pays off the debt in mana crystals. An elder shaman arrives with the lion-maned man and demands that Ken and Feline stay. Ken portals Alice's group out with Charlotte, Dez, and Penny, while he and Feline follow the shaman.

So far this book: In the shaman's hall, Feline reveals that Ken was a human until a dungeon item turned him into a demon. He immediately loses the protection the cat-people give to demons, and a lion-type guard attacks. The shaman plans to reeducate Feline in her goddess's faith and pair her with a mate from the guard's clan, noting that fewer than a hundred older Spirit Tigers remain. When Ken tries to portal out with Feline, the shaman breaks both his legs. Locked in a house, Ken heals himself with a potion and portals to Halen, where Crimson immediately offers to kill whoever hurt him. Crimson heals him, and Ken brings in his grandparents instead of launching a full assault. His grandmother buffs the team with a war banner, Crimson draws attention as a distraction, and Ken and his grandfather sneak in. The lion-type guard breaks their camouflage. He explains that orc-like observers enforce honor rules and that Ken's invasion now lets him fight freely. Ken breaks the guard's shield arm, smashes his potion, and kills him with help from Feline's ice and lightning. Feline takes the guard's wrist device, which the cat-people use instead of a CID. Ken then joins Crimson against the shaman, who is above level 80. The shaman calls down a giant finger that wipes out half the safe zone, but Ken breaks her barrier with Arcane Singularity and kills her with Mana Implosion. Back at the Star City house, Dez and Charlotte heal the wounded, and Crimson forbids the party from going back to the settlement.

So far this book: The UG president and directors question Ken and Crimson about the destroyed safe zone, but an orc-like arbiter takes over and says the UG cannot punish Crimson. Ken admits that demon blood made him a demon, turns down an offer to be studied, and hands over the cat-person wrist disc, which supports his account that the cat-people attacked first. In a private interview, the arbiter warns Feline that her shrinking tribe may try to claim her. He finds Ken and Crimson guilty of excessive violence and assigns their side 31 percent of the blame, along with loot rights on the dead shaman. The party agrees to share the debt because Feline is one of them. Feline and Ken become intimate. With Ambrosia's guidance they shop at Star City's projection hubs, where Ken sells Shadow Strike and buys the upgraded Shadow Claw. Two weeks of farming zombies on floor 46 pays off about 60 percent of their share. Classes resume at Halen without Fayeth, and Crimson teaches the class, adding exploration and civics for dealing with foreign races. In an essay exercise on a goblin floor, Penny ends up in Ken's lap with Dez's help, and Ken tells Penny he is interested in her. Classmates offer to help with the debt but cut back their pledges once they hear the amount. Feline thanks them and says she may need to find her own people somewhere else.

So far this book: After two weeks of lessons, Harley reports that two surviving parties from the 40th floor were pulled out by Royal Academy elites. On a free weekend, Ken, Penny, and Feline meet a curious six-armed Naga matriarch in Star City, who thinks Ken is a dwarf and takes them to watch an angels' bathhouse. Ambrosia covers for Ken when he is caught looking. She tells them she wants to leave the city and learn to dive, and Ken and Penny offer to send her to Halen, with Ken paying her tuition. Penny shows open jealousy, and Ken praises both her looks and her writing. Ken and Penny visit the guild hall, where the young-looking succubus Mel greets Ken as a fellow demon. Ken registers the Silverfangs and makes Penny a member. His outdated CID can only be read through the hall's own system. Dez passes along that Penny's father needs her, and Ken and Penny fight their way to his safe zone. Her father, Roger, explains that SJS, now run by another royal, has bought up his debts as part of a rush to grab safe zones. Ken agrees to take over the 200-million debt, and SJS threatens to destroy the safe zone. Ken tells Roger he is dating Penny. On their tavern date, Penny says she does not mind Ken's other partners. Then a wounded diver arrives and reports that about forty Naga killed his party two floors below. Ken realizes his CID cannot reach Crimson or Dez.

So far this book: Ken carries Penny down to floor 23, where they destroy two Naga hunting parties and then a stronger group with a healer. After that, a level 43 formation forces them into a fighting retreat toward the stairs. Ken clears the Naga holding the stairs and finds the UG fighters above scattered by a level 51 Naga matriarch. She heals, casts buffs, and fights with two flamberges, but Ken uses the speed from his trial to overcome the seven-level gap and kills her with Mana Implosion. The invasion collapses. Roger gives Ken his blessing to date Penny, which makes Ken uneasy because it sounds like approval for marriage. About two hours after the attack began, a UG force arrives with the UG director, Selene's mother. She gives Ken and Penny the largest share of the bounty and notes that SJS keeps buying safe zones the Naga have raided. Suspecting human collusion, she hires the Nagato clan to investigate SJS and trace the Naga route. Ken agrees and suggests capturing Naga for the friendly Star City matriarch to question. He chooses the rare Sword of Omens stun as his reward, and Penny takes a unique frost orb.

So far this book: Ken, Penny, Feline, Ambrosia, and the friendly Naga matriarch follow the raiders' route with Eyes of Wisdom. On floor 28 the matriarch questions red-tribe Naga, who only found the path a day earlier. The group suspects SJS, which has been helping remap the dungeon since the shuffle. A red matriarch refuses to give up her human contacts until Ken brings Crimson through a portal and the Naga back down. They hand over a serpent-eye device used to talk with the humans. From the new SJS president's point of view, he is planning smear campaigns against the families of Ken's friends when the device activates, and the friendly matriarch, posing as the raiders' leader, draws him out. Ken comes through a portal with the UG director, her husband, and their allies. The husband subdues the president, and under questioning he admits that the Kai Ming assassins worked for SJS and that Ken's mother refused to make the Nagato clan an SJS tool. Penny keeps Ken from killing him outright. Ken beheads him and then revives him to show he is not untouchable. The director takes him into UG custody.

So far this book: Ken and Penny stay at a UG hotel in the safe zone, where they begin a sexual relationship and Penny agrees to be one of his partners. Back in class, Crimson opens a UG-funded gravity training room in Star City. She explains that the class gained ten levels without much stat training and splits the students into healers, tanks, and damage dealers. The damage team loses, Ken collapses after building too many Liminal Speed stacks, and Dez revives him. Crimson reveals she is level 67, and the sessions grow to about eight hours. Two orc-like guild members recognize Ken's speed and Crimson's limit break as rewards from trials. They say there are seven trials and that the seven cities were built on them. At the guild hall, Mel says that trials usually lie between floors 75 and 85, that few people survive them, and that a trial skill is almost necessary to go past floor 100. She names four trial colors: red for power, purple for speed, green for thorns and reflection, and blue for mana. Ken and Crimson confirm that Eyes of Wisdom can find trials and agree to keep that secret. The UG director and UG president then give Ken a list of SJS associates still alive, saying that removing them will prevent retaliation and keep things stable.

Through the end: Working alone and without telling his party, Ken kills two names on the list of five. He then captures the most central figure, a Kai Ming liaison, in a safe-zone brothel. The man reveals that SJS planted agents in most of Ken's mother's party to turn her and the Nagato clan, and that a later SJS leader decided to let the clan wither. Ken kills him despite having promised not to. At the Nagato estate, one of his grandmothers makes him rest, criticizes him for acting alone, tells him to share the list with the clan, and sends for Crimson. Ken leaves jewelry at his parents' shrine. Crimson scolds him and brings him to a mountain hideaway. She suggests the UG gave him the mission to keep his revenge under control, tells him to refuse UG work until the school year and summer are over and come to her instead, and says she will push the party toward the trials next year. Ken invites Dez to the hideaway. His sheet shows level 45 at 27 percent, the Emperor class, the Silverfangs guild, and the Speed trial. In secret, Crimson trains alone in the gravity room, worried that Ken will overtake her.

characters.description: The narrator and heir of the Nagato clan, a human whose incubus form was granted by the dungeon, although Star City assumes he was born a demon. An Emperor-class melee fighter, he ends a summer of private gravity-chamber training with Crimson exhausted and aware that he still trails the strongest fighters. Before leaving the chamber he agrees to a future duel with a young orc-like warrior who mocks him as a little demon.
characters.name: Ken

characters.description: The strongest human, a Halen instructor, and Ken's lover and private trainer. Since the Naga attack and humanity's arrival in Star City she has quietly pushed her own training harder. She passes on research suggesting one day of diving for every four of training, and reminds Ken that his grandmother expects the clan heir to train with the new recruits.
characters.name: Crimson

characters.description: A young warrior of the orc-like race that dominates Star City, belonging to one of the city's guilds. He shoulders past Ken outside the gravity chamber, calls him a little demon, and demands proof of strength, drawing Ken into an agreement to duel him in the gravity chambers at a later date.
characters.name: Orc-like guild fighter

characters.description: A young cat-person shaman, son of his clan's chief shaman. His grandmother, the clan's elder shaman, died fighting an incubus in an earlier dispute, and his sister lies unconscious in the healing ward still believing the grandmother lived. Lucian despises incubi, and with his father's quiet encouragement he starts looking for indirect ways to strike at the incubus, such as leaving him unable to pay the fine the arbiters imposed.
characters.name: Lucian

characters.description: Chief shaman of Lucian's clan, a cold and formidable figure around level 90 or higher. He tells his son that the orc-like arbiters found both sides at fault in the clash that killed the clan's elder shaman, so only a fine applies. Unable to move openly, he hints that Lucian should work through others and make the incubus unable to pay.
characters.name: Lucian's father

characters.description: Lucian's sister, lying in a coma in her clan's healing ward. She believes their grandmother survived the fight with the incubus, and Lucian lets her keep that belief. She is the family member he plainly cares for, in contrast to their cold parents.
characters.name: Lucian's sister

characters.description: Ken's grandfather, an aging swordsman who fights with a sword of light. He welcomes Ken home with a surprise attack, and Ken, now his equal or slightly better in speed, beats him using liminal space. Playful and secretly glad to see his grandson, he is teased by the household about his several wives and a hidden stash.
characters.name: Ken's grandfather

characters.description: Ken's masked, white-haired servant, a butler with the manner of a ninja, returning from earlier books. When Ken comes home Ami walks him through the rebuilt Nagato clan and explains the many young recruits who have joined it.
characters.name: Ami

characters.description: One of Ken's partners and a member of his party. She comes from a warlock family with demon blood, became a demon herself in the previous book, and now fights as a demonic mage with a heart-shaped pupil. She joins Ken in greeting guests at the clan's welcome feast and swaps summer stories with Penny and Charlotte.
characters.name: Dez

characters.description: A white-haired, blue-striped shaman of the spirit tiger tribe and a member of Ken's party. Her people split from the main cat-person clans long ago and worship the dungeon, which tribes devoted to the goddess Neko regard as heresy. A clan kidnapped her after the shuffle. Her CID functions through her rituals.
characters.name: Feline

characters.description: Ken's partner and the party's healer, owner of the dungeon monster Bun-Bun. She has become more confident and bolder in public over the summer. During the clan's welcome feast she helps out in the kitchen with Penny before joining the others.
characters.name: Charlotte

characters.description: One of Ken's companions and the party's tank, who has grown as strong as her own father over the summer. She helps in the kitchen at the clan's welcome feast and compares summers with Charlotte and Dez.
characters.name: Penny

characters.description: Charlotte's pet, a dungeon monster roughly as strong as Charlotte herself. He ambushes Ken at the welcome feast and is handled with good humor.
characters.name: Bun-Bun

characters.description: Helen's mother, a powerful human adventurer widely known as the harem queen, reported to be in the upper 60s in level. She is actively pursuing information about trials, with Helen accompanying her.
characters.name: Harem queen

characters.description: A red-haired paladin in Ken's class at Halen and the daughter of the harem queen. She spent the summer training with her mother and remains openly hostile toward Ken, even while trading gossip with him and Harley before class.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: A pink-haired bard in Ken's class who jokes about wanting a harem of healers and is always eager to pry into gossip.
characters.name: Harley

characters.description: One of Ken's classmates, an anxious perfectionist who takes assignments and grades very seriously.
characters.name: Candice

characters.description: A black-winged angel shunned by other angels and kept in employment by Crimson. She greets Ken's class when it arrives in Star City to see the new Halen building.
characters.name: Ambrosia

characters.description: Head of a guild of the orc-like host race and a steady, methodical tank whom Ken is scheduled to duel. Outside the gravity chambers he questions Ken and the class, acting more like an interviewer than his usual swaggering self, and proposes that Ken's guild be ranked through a sparring match watched by observers. When Dez boasts about the size and strength of Ken's harem, he takes it as a slip revealing that Ken hides his real power.
characters.name: Orc-like guild leader

characters.description: A courteous whale-tailed man about eight feet tall, with fin-shaped ears and a huge anchor as his weapon. He trips a wire at the class's dungeon camp at night, addresses Ken as an incubus, and politely asks the way to his destination.
characters.name: Whale-people anchor

characters.description: A small, blue-haired woman in the whale-people party who fills the pillar role in their two-role formation of anchors and pillars. Blunt, loud and very strong, she lives outside any pod, is startled to see a cat-person and a demon paired as mates, bickers with Feline over fish, and quickly befriends Dez.
characters.name: Whale-people pillar

characters.description: A senior arbiter of the orc-like host race whose power is so far beyond Ken's that a scan reads above level 100 and returns errors. When a local attacks one of his guards in a safe zone under investigation, he treats the act as an admission of guilt and erases the zone's central buildings and everyone inside with a single strike.
characters.name: Senior arbiter

characters.description: An elderly, cheerful official of the orc-like host race who steps in at the end of Ken's duel. A retired arbiter now handling administrative work, he still carries the standing of a judge. He re-registers Ken, keeps his stats and skills off the record, rates him only on what the fight displayed, and reminds him that justice has no borders.
characters.name: Retired arbiter

characters.description: Head of the UG, a scarred man Crimson refers to by a nickname. As the UG sets up offices in Star City and pledges support to the arbiters, he receives Ken and several classmates summoned to the UG and shows them to a meeting.
characters.name: UG president

characters.description: The elf princess and future empress, whom the elves already count as Ken's wife. She attends the meeting about marking Ken's followers and supports extending the mark through his organizations, the elves included, while preparing to explain why placing her people under Ken could serve them.
characters.name: Ellie

characters.description: An elf ally of Ken's from earlier books who supports her people. She is present at the meeting in the elven palace where Ken's partners discuss marking his followers.
characters.name: Fayeth

characters.description: A senior elf censor who attends the meeting at the elven palace with a second censor while the elves weigh accepting Ken's mark.
characters.name: Chief censor

characters.description: A cloaked, dark-skinned enforcer adopted into Lucian's clan, with only his eyes showing. He drags Lucian back to the chieftain after the failed attack on Ken, answers directly to the chieftain, and is assigned to keep watch over the disgraced Lucian.
characters.name: Lucian's guard

characters.description: A younger elf censor who was thrown onto floors in the 90s during the shuffle and survived by resting and relying on a travel ability, encountering whales and demons along the way. Crimson located her with Eyes of Wisdom and the chief censor brought her home. She receives Ken's mark on her shoulder.
characters.name: Second censor

characters.description: The public relations manager for the Nagato clan and the Silver Fangs, who wears the Silver Fangs mark over her heart. She arrives at the class's trial site with a camera crew, interviews Ken about the trial, and teasingly calls him her sugar daddy on camera.
characters.name: PR manager

characters.description: An elderly woman with white, blue-striped ears and tail who leads the Spirit Tiger clan and carries authority over other cat-person clan heads. At a council of clan chiefs she breaks the limbs of Lucian's father and explains what little is known about the worms that revive dead hosts.
characters.name: Spirit Tiger chief

characters.description: A red-lipped demoness with the rank of demon lord who leads a delegation of a dozen or more demons, including an imp and a large bearded demon, to Star City by a newly discovered route from their home city. She has fought the retired arbiter in the past, and her group must be tested for worms on arrival.
characters.name: Demon lord

recaps.ending: Lucian is dead, beheaded by Ken during the ambush at the crystal whale trial. His clan guard, revived once by a fount of life ability and then beaten by Crimson, is in arbiter custody on thirty-two counts of aggression. Lucian's father has been broken by the Spirit Tiger chief and detained with the rest of his clan's leaders, and other clans are told to give them no help, though Ken still worries about what the wider cat-person race may do. Ken is level 52, back in Star City under arbiter watch, facing a test, assigned reading, and another dive, and still hiding the full reach of Eyes of Wisdom. Crimson, Dez, Charlotte, Feline, Penny, Helen, Bun-Bun and the class are all alive after revivals. Feline has completed the whale trial and carries its blue-lightning power. Ken's crown-of-daggers mark binds his harem, the Nagato clan, part of the Silver Fangs and two elf censors to his demon hierarchy, but Penny has not yet taken hers, and Charlotte's hoped-for wedding is still ahead. The harem queen is now an ally and co-teacher, bargaining with Crimson for trial locations, while Crimson keeps paying down her debt to the arbiters with help from Ken's grandfather. Helen denies any feelings for Ken despite her mother's claims. The elves remain at war with the Naga and their dark-elf allies, and the censors' limit break trial is unresolved. The worms called Threadspawn are a new race whose origin and purpose are unknown and which ordinary methods cannot detect. The whale-people remain friendly, the UG keeps pressing to stand between humans and the arbiters, and a delegation of demons led by a demon lord has just reached Star City.
recaps.in_short: Ken Nagato returns for another year of training under Crimson, now held in Star City among the orc-like host race. He wins an assessed duel against an orc-like guild tank and is registered by a retired arbiter who hides his stats, but Lucian, a cat-person shaman whose grandmother died fighting Ken, declares himself Ken's enemy over Feline. Lucian's trap on a graveyard floor nearly kills the class until the harem queen and the UG president intervene. Learning that a demon mark can bind followers to him, Ken tattoos his harem, clan, guild members and two elf censors with a crown of daggers, while the elves face war with the Naga and a race resembling dark elves. For their midterm the class must win trial abilities, and while they challenge a crystal whale, Lucian strikes again with mercenaries secretly controlled by reviving worms. Helen and several classmates die before being revived, Ken kills Lucian, Crimson subdues Lucian's guard, and Feline completes the trial. The arbiters name the worms Threadspawn, clear the class, and detain Lucian's clan leaders, and the book closes as a demon delegation led by a demon lord arrives in Star City.

recaps.text: Previously: Ken Nagato, heir to the Nagato clan, was turned into an incubus by the dungeon and holds the Emperor class. He trains under Crimson, the strongest human, who is also his lover, and he keeps a closely guarded secret: his Eyes of Wisdom skill can locate trials, the challenges that award powerful abilities, and he has already completed the Trial of Speed. His party includes his companions Dez, Charlotte and Penny along with Feline, a shaman of the spirit tiger tribe, and the elves, including the elf princess and Fayeth, are close allies. After the shuffle reshaped the dungeon, a cat-person clan kidnapped Feline. In the dispute that followed, the clan's elder shaman died fighting Ken, and the orc-like arbiters ruled both sides at fault and left Ken owing a fine. Dez became a demon herself and took up the path of a demonic mage. Humanity survived a Naga attack in which Ken fought the Naga matriarch, and then reached Star City, a hub governed by an orc-like host race where humans are newcomers and Ken is taken for a born demon. Helen's mother, a powerful adventurer known as the harem queen, once saved Ken's class from a dwarven queen. Ken begins the new school year famous at home but still far below the dungeon's strongest powers.

So far this book: Ken wraps up a summer of private gravity training with Crimson in Star City, where she shares research favoring one dungeon day for every four of training. Outside the chamber a young orc-like guild fighter mocks him as a little demon, and Ken agrees to a duel. Elsewhere, the cat-person shaman Lucian keeps watch over his comatose sister; their grandmother was the elder shaman who died fighting Ken. His father, the clan's chief shaman, cannot act openly but nudges Lucian to work through others and keep the incubus from paying the arbiters' fine. Ken returns to the Nagato estate, wins a surprise bout with his grandfather using liminal space, and tours the growing clan with his servant Ami. At a welcome feast he reunites with Dez, Feline, Charlotte, Penny and Bun-Bun, and hears that the harem queen is hunting trial information. Ken's party then returns to campus at Halen. Elsewhere, in the dungeon, Lucian's group overpowers a team of orc-like warriors and questions the guild fighter, learning about the duel and the cat-person shaman in Ken's party, whom Lucian intends to take back. In class, Crimson sets every other party against Ken's five at once. Ken's party wins, Dez charms the healers, and Ken defeats Helen, who swears a rematch once she earns a trial skill. Crimson punishes the class with laps over an invented summer assignment, the harem queen arrives, and the class moves to a new Halen building in Star City, where Ambrosia greets them and the headmistress appears to scold Crimson and Ken.

So far this book: Lessons settle into classroom mornings, gravity-chamber afternoons and a dive every third day. An orc-like guild leader, the tank Ken is set to duel, quizzes the class and suggests ranking Ken's guild through an observed match; Dez's boasting about Ken's harem convinces him Ken is concealing his strength. Ken chases a spy through the streets without catching him. Crimson notes that Ken is level 50 but poorly geared, and Ambrosia, her angel servant, describes her contract. On a weekend dive, a party of five whale-people wanders into the class's camp. Their polite, anchor-wielding leader takes Ken for an ordinary demon, and their small blue-haired pillar reveals an old grudge between cat-people and demons. The next morning they demonstrate their anchor-and-pillar formation, killing Ken and Penny in practice before both are revived, then head for Star City. Claiming Crimson chose the route, Ken secretly follows a path from Eyes of Wisdom that points toward the nearest trial, and the class goes along. On a level 49 floor of zombies and hydra roosters, the floor boss, a three-headed rooster that turns into a regenerating hydra, falls to Ken's party, and he shares the tactics so every group clears it. In the safe zone beyond, arbiters are investigating, and when a local strikes a guard, a senior arbiter above level 100 obliterates the zone's center and everyone in it with one blow. Shaken, the class resolves to keep leveling. Meanwhile Lucian corners the guild leader in a tavern for information about Ken, and the frightened leader arranges observers for the coming duel.

So far this book: On duel day, Dez's mother and the harem queen join Ken and Crimson at the gravity chambers for a guild ranking assessment. Ken senses killing intent from one of three lion-like cat-people in the audience, and a connection between them and his opponent. An elderly orc-like assessor opens the bout against the guild leader, a patient tank whose trial ability, Absolute Reflect, stores damage as green lightning and unleashes it in one burst. Ken drains him with Shadow Limb and Mana Burn, takes True Demon Form, and lands Mana Implosion, though the reflected flash blinds him. Ken wins, leaving the tank kneeling with a severe wound. A retired arbiter who now serves as a judge re-registers Ken, hides his stats and skills, and grades him only on what he showed, and Ken unveils a new skill, Sovereign's Mandate. Ken states on record that a hostile watcher belongs to the clan he faced in arbitration. Lucian then introduces himself as the grandson of the shaman who died trying to take Feline, offers to buy her, gets slapped, and vows to free her. The whale-people explain how much a judge's opinion matters and urge Ken to stay in safe zones. Feline runs off in tears; Ken catches her with Shadow Ambush and refuses to let her go, and she resolves to become strong enough to save him one day. Crimson recommends random dive sites, and the retired arbiter privately warns that the arbiters may wipe out every side in a dispute and that Ken should not fight Lucian's clan.

So far this book: Crimson moves the class onto a harsher regime. The UG, newly established in Star City, announces it will back the orc-like arbiters and act as go-between for humans. Ken and several top classmates are summoned; the harem queen greets Ken as a suitor for Helen, which he denies. The scarred UG president asks them to let the UG handle discipline and channel arbitration payments. The group stays silent when asked to re-register with the UG, and Ken wants guilds to pay directly. He says he will defend humans from outside attack but will not shelter anyone who starts their own fights. The harem queen warns that the arbiters have turned reckless, offers help, and is surprised to hear Helen supposedly dislikes Ken. The defeated guild leader admits Lucian forced him to talk. After weeks of training, a UG alert reports the White Tigers Guild in danger. Ken portals the class to a graveyard on floor 48, sends fallen White Tigers back, and walks into Lucian's trap. A suppression field pins the class while Lucian stabs Dez and burns Charlotte with lightning. Ken breaks loose with True Demon Form and Arcane Singularity, then activates Sovereign's Mandate, drawing power from his party and many distant bonds. A hooded, high-level clansman sent by Lucian's father breaks Ken's arm and Lucian drives a staff into his chest, but Ken tears Lucian's throat with Shadow Claw. Through Ken's portal come the harem queen and her men, then the UG president with Valkyrie summons, and the clansman retreats with Lucian. Crimson and Ken agree to keep the arbiters out of it, and the harem queen offers to teach Ken how to train his harem-based power.

So far this book: Crimson sends Ken and Helen to the 69th floor, where the harem queen runs a training operation around her large harem. She explains that strength drawn from followers scales with their number and level, urges Ken to widen his circle, and teases Helen about her supposed attraction to him. A book on demons shows Ken holds the lowest demon rank and that a mark such as a tattoo can permanently place followers under him, adding Emperor bonuses at the risk that a future superior demon could command them. Ambrosia reports a small army of Lucian's people in Star City and a vague arbiter travel warning. At a harem meeting at the elven palace, run by Dez, the group chooses a crown of daggers as the mark. The elf princess reveals that the elves are at full war with the Naga, whose new allies resemble legendary dark elves at level 90 to 100, so her people would welcome demonic protection. Lucian's father beats him for failing, Lucian's two party mates are executed under clan law, and, learning the arbiters are occupied deep in the dungeon, the father orders Lucian to kill Ken, his women and his human allies. Ken marks Charlotte first, then Dez, Crimson, Feline, Fayeth and the elf princess, while Penny postpones hers. Charlotte and Ken talk of a wedding. The two elf censors accept the mark, all 69 Nagato clan members follow, and 28 Silver Fangs agree. Crimson is working off her debt to the arbiters, and Ken reaches level 52. For the midterm, Crimson and the harem queen require every student to earn a trial ability; Ken passes automatically and will guide his class there by portal.

So far this book: More than a week into a dive, the class reaches a trial on a level 57 forest floor, shaped like a floating crystal whale. Candice identifies its reward as boundless mana, which boosts spell power, cost and regeneration in proportion to mana pool. Only one challenger may fight at a time, and the whale heals within seconds. Candice's rune turrets do the most damage before she collapses from exhaustion, and Dez builds her mana by letting Ken drain her. Helen, who brought a portable gravity chamber, rejects her mother's claims about her and calls the tattoos demonic slavery, which Ken disputes. Elsewhere the two elf censors attempt a limit break trial Crimson found for them, and Crimson sells the harem queen the location of an Absolute Reflect trial for mana crystals and a promise to treat Ken well. The whale-people anchor and a whale-people woman join the class, explaining that their people favor the fount of life and limit break abilities. Ken's PR manager arrives to film the attempts. Lucian, unable to use his father's guard openly, bribes his way to a strange mercenary crew in a remote safe zone, watches a stream of Ken's group, and pays the crew to find the trial floor; the guard keeps quiet in exchange for being allowed to kill the crew's clanless leader afterward. When the whale finally cracks, a crystal shark emerges and kills Dez, who is revived. Feline begins her own attempt with lightning-charged arrows and spears, and a perimeter alarm sounds as a man in a red cap steps out of the trees.

So far this book: The stranger claims to be human but answers strangely, and Eyes of Wisdom reveal hidden figures in the forest. Lucian's mercenaries attack while the whale-people hold one flank. The stranger dissolves Ken's portal, and slain mercenaries keep rising. Ken sends the PR manager to his Star City house; an infected host follows, and an arbiter crushes its head and extracts a worm. Helen dies shielding Ken, Lucian's guard heals Lucian, and cat-people pin down the arbiter. The guard kills several classmates, including Harley and Taylor. Using True Demon Form, Arcane Singularity and Sovereign's Mandate, Ken kills Lucian and takes his head, then beheads the guard, who returns through a fount of life ability. Crimson arrives and defeats the guard. Feline completes the whale trial, crackling with blue lightning, and shows that beheading a host and removing its worm stops the revivals, so the mercenaries are destroyed. Ken and Crimson free the arbiter and kill his attackers, and Ken revives his fallen classmates. The arbiter rules that Ken's quarrel is with Lucian's clan alone, takes the guard into custody on thirty-two counts of aggression, and names the worms Threadspawn. Ken secretly uses Eyes of Wisdom to find worms in three bodies, and orc-like scientists clear the class. At a council of clan heads, the Spirit Tiger chief breaks Lucian's father's limbs and the arbiters detain his clan's leaders. In a Star City tavern, Helen, alive again, insists she was only keeping Ken alive. Ken weighs the worms, the dark elves and the cat-people, and the book ends as a demon delegation led by a demon lord arrives by a new route, welcomed by the retired arbiter and sent for worm testing.

characters.description: The first-person narrator, a third-year student in a class tied to the Silver Fangs guild. He was once human and became an incubus after taking in demon blood that his teacher Crimson had gathered, blood that also made a dungeon boss far more dangerous. Since a recent ambush he has been limited to classes and city life, because dungeon trips are suspended while mind-controlling worms are loose. Investigators have confirmed that no one in his class is under worm control.
characters.name: Ken

characters.description: The narrator's girlfriend and classmate, who fights as a demonic mage. She started life as a human and is now a demon. Like the rest of their Silver Fangs class, she is kept out of the dungeon for the time being while the mind-controlling worms remain at large.
characters.name: Dez

characters.description: The class's teacher and the strongest human adventurer alive. She has black hair and blue eyes, wears red leather cut from a monster-dinosaur hide, goes by Mistress Crimson after her surname, and flirts with the narrator openly. She collected the demon blood that turned him into an incubus. Under pressure from the college, the United Guilds, and students' families, she has halted dungeon trips because of the loose worms and a deep-dungeon race hunting anyone who might be possessed, but she is lining up chaperones so the class can hunt the trial monsters it needs during a surface job fair.
characters.name: Crimson

characters.description: A blonde, studious classmate who likes rules to be followed. She protests when Crimson has the students mark one another's tests instead of grading them herself, unaware until the narrator lets it slip that Crimson has been awarding her full marks without reading her work.
characters.name: Candace

characters.description: A paladin classmate with fiery hair who disapproves of harems, an attitude the narrator puts down to trouble with her parents. She belongs to the class's Silver Fangs group but is one of the few members not set on staying with the guild.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: A cat-like Nekorian who lives in the narrator's Star City household, a home Crimson also shares. Around the house she is known for preferring meat dishes when the residents cook.
characters.name: Cat-race companion

characters.description: A small, pigtailed succubus the narrator knows, usually trailed by admirers from the orc-eyed deep-dungeon race. She passes on word that a succubus demon lord has arrived in Star City with a retinue and is rumored to be connected to the worms.
characters.name: Succubus acquaintance

characters.description: A former top influencer who now runs public relations for the Silver Fangs guild, working mostly with Crimson. Because the college leadership has kept Crimson away from the press, she is assigned to manage the publicity tour meant to reassure the public about the college.
characters.name: Silver Fangs PR manager

characters.description: The head of the college, a gray-haired former adventurer in a purple robe whose own students have outgrown her in level. She once tried to have the narrator expelled for failing and remains openly hostile to him and to Crimson. She briefs the press-tour students to represent the school well and keep their answers vague on sensitive subjects. Candace's mother does business with her.
characters.name: Headmistress

characters.description: Known publicly as the harem queen, she is a red-haired Halen teacher, Helen's mother, and an ally of the narrator, and is said to be more popular than Crimson. She turns up as a surprise podcast guest, recounts her battle with a dwarf queen at the 25th-floor safe zone while crediting the narrator with the killing blow, and teases him about joining her harem to her daughter's embarrassment.
characters.name: Heather

characters.description: The narrator's grandmother, who stays in contact by message during the press tour. When the group guesses at the identity of a secret podcast guest, she confirms that the narrator's grandfather, a member of the first raid to go beyond level 30, will not be appearing.
characters.name: Ken's grandmother

characters.description: A dwarven queen who invades New York, sending swarms of mindless drone workers into buildings and a studio. She commands both the drones and a more intelligent warrior caste, and is found on the roof of Grand Central Station directing her drones to raise a fortress when Ken's group arrives to stop her.
characters.name: Dwarven queen

characters.description: A cameraman who records the battle in Grand Central Station. A low-level adventurer thanks to a friend, he watches Ken move faster than any human should and understands that his footage shows what deep-diving adventurers turn into.
characters.name: Kevin

characters.description: The head of the United Guilds, a big, scarred man whom Crimson regards as a coward. He questions Ken and Heather after the New York fight, reveals that Crimson is using Ken's shared detection ability to screen high-level teams for worm hosts, and explains that the infected will be captured and studied in a facility. He also advises Ken to keep clear of the demons, who rank humans near the bottom.
characters.name: UG president

characters.description: A flattering talk show host with a wealthy social circle. On his show the audience adores Ken, who slices Gary's cup with a short sword without using abilities. Gary invites the group to his after-party, and Ken accepts.
characters.name: Gary

characters.description: A member of Ken's party who joins the group as they dress for Gary's party in New York and goes with them to the ballroom.
characters.name: Penny

characters.description: A member of Ken's party who joins the group as they get ready for Gary's party and attends the ballroom gathering with them.
characters.name: Charlotte

characters.description: One of Ken's companions, a blue-haired woman of a whale-like race with ears shaped like fins. She knows little about human society and is puzzled when Ken explains carrying, where strong players haul rich low-level clients. She finds it hard to believe that Ken was ever human.
characters.name: Whale-race companion

characters.description: A blue-haired director who is second-in-command of the United Guilds, brisk and efficient. When Ken cannot reach the president, she promises UG staff for the infected adventurers he has found and asks him to subdue them so they can be studied.
characters.name: UG director

characters.description: A gaunt blonde woman with a hole in her abdomen who sits in a large tub filled with thousands of loose worms in a castle-like New York penthouse. Though human, she is a worm host of overwhelming strength, drops two of Ken's companions with a glance, and shrugs off every ability he has. She seems to lead the infected in New York.
characters.name: New York worm host

characters.description: A black-winged angel who lives in the Star City apartment Ken shares with Crimson. Her own race shuns her for wearing black. She treats visitors courteously and tells Ken that Crimson has gone out for a drink.
characters.name: Ambrosia

characters.description: A succubus demon lord with a crown of horns, golden eyes, and a spaded tail. Her subordinates call her mistress, and outsiders address her as lady or lord. Politically sharp and dangerous, she quickly realizes Ken is not a born demon when he enters her building, asks whether he carries a worm, and accuses him of pretending to be a demon.
characters.name: Lady Frey

characters.description: A pink-haired demon princess who appears at the New York penthouse once the worm host is subdued. Lady Frey defers to her, and she seems to know who Ken is. She burns the tub of worms, sears the host's gut with a small flame, offers Ken a steed contract that he turns down, and takes the captive away.
characters.name: Pink-haired demon princess

characters.description: An incubus who is a rival candidate for the empty incubus throne. Lady Frey calls Ken through her stone while he is in the dungeon and orders him to kill this rival.
characters.name: Rival incubus

characters.description: An aged succubus who welcomes Ken and Dez warmly at a royal demon gathering in the Sloth Queen's palace and puts Lady Frey at ease. She is the Succubus Queen, who ranks above the princess Frey serves.
characters.name: Succubus Queen

characters.description: A large succubus of high standing who attends the royal demon gathering. Together with the pink-haired princess, she backs Ken and shields him while he scans the crowd for worm carriers.
characters.name: Large succubus lady

characters.description: The orc-like leader of a mixed band of non-humans, including a naga, an elf, and a demon, who ambush Ken during his press tour. The attackers have the unnatural strength of worm hosts, and their leader speaks for the parasites as a whole. He demands that Ken come with them for his sight or watch everyone he cares about be taken, before the pink-haired princess pins the group and carries him off.
characters.name: Orc-like parasite envoy

characters.description: A member of Ken's class whom his scan reveals to be carrying a worm. She is the daughter of a United Guilds director. Ken's party argues over whether to kill her or capture her and decides to try to help her without the UG.
characters.name: Infected classmate

characters.description: An overworked doctor at the United Guilds facility where the infected are held. He treats the disguised party members smuggled in as patients and takes orders from a figure with a smoky voice who calls the worm hosts siblings.
characters.name: Facility doctor

characters.description: A huge, axe-wielding orc-like worm host who confronts Ken and Crimson near the dungeon entrance. He says Ken killed his relative, the breeder in the bathtub, speaks about how highly the parasites value family, and badly wounds Ken in the fight that follows.
characters.name: Orc-like worm host

recaps.ending: Ken closes the book as a demon general and the Succubus Queen's favored candidate for the incubus throne, bound by his contract with Lady Frey to yearly service, mana crystal payments, and a steep repayment rate on any help she gives. The pink-haired princess who serves the Imp King manages his scanning work and is his main protector, while the Succubus Queen has publicly staked her reputation on him. His exposure of the infected Asura prince, his killing of a rival incubus, and his defeat of a demon prince's hit squad (the imp leader killed and the other four captured) have left him with enemies among the demons, and the parasites themselves have openly targeted him for his sight. He has chosen to keep a predictable schedule as bait so they come after him instead of his people. His relationship with the United Guilds is broken: the president refuses to share cure research, Crimson was turned away from the UG facility, and Crimson suspects but cannot confirm that the president may be infected. Crimson has resolved to destroy the parasite nest on Earth. Dez holds demon blood and a research tome she plans to use to strengthen herself. The facility doctor is dead and his lab ruined, though his first patient lived, and Ken has shown he can cut a worm out of a living host in liminal time, saving his classmate. Heather arrives at the end and sees what he has done. Still unresolved are how to scale the cure, the remaining parasites on Earth, the infected possibly lurking within the UG, retaliation from the demon prince, the class's trial on floor 58, and the fate of the New York host after her capture.
recaps.in_short: Barred from the dungeon while mind-controlling worms spread, Ken is sent on a press tour with Dez, Helen, Candace, and the Silver Fangs PR manager, who becomes his lover. In New York he and Heather kill a worm-infected dwarven queen, then Ken uses Eyes of Wisdom to capture infected humans for the United Guilds, including fighters at a society death-match event. A worm-breeding host in a New York penthouse proves far stronger than him, so he seeks help from the succubus lord Lady Frey, who exposes his human origin and signs him as her candidate for the vacant incubus throne. Frey and Crimson subdue the host, and a pink-haired demon princess takes her away. Ken kills a rival incubus and defeats the squad sent after him, killing its imp leader and capturing the rest, then scans a royal gathering in hell and exposes an infected Asura prince, setting off a purge. The UG cuts him off, and parasites attack him in public demanding his sight. When a classmate turns out to be infected, Ken, Crimson, and the party infiltrate a parasite-controlled UG facility, defeat a giant worm mass formed around an orc-like host, and lose the doctor seeking a cure. Ken finally removes his classmate's worm himself in liminal time, and she survives as Heather arrives.

recaps.text:
So far this book: The class sits an exam on deep-dungeon races and the demon hierarchy, including the rule that a demon prince can only rise to king by helping their lord kill a rival ruler. Crimson keeps her students out of the dungeon because mind-controlling worms are loose, a deep-dungeon race is hunting anyone who might be possessed, and the college, the United Guilds, and families are pressing her. She plans a surface job fair with chaperoned hunts so the class can still face the trial monsters it needs.

While sparring in a gravity chamber, Crimson tells the narrator that the headmistress has picked him, his demonic-mage girlfriend, Candace, and the paladin for a publicity tour meant to reassure people. The Silver Fangs PR manager will run it because Crimson is barred from the press. Enrollment has fallen about a fifth. A succubus acquaintance reports that a succubus demon lord with a retinue has reached Star City and may be tied to the worms. The narrator has never told demons he was born human, and an incubus missing from demon records could be suspected of possession, so the tour also buys time.

After a frosty briefing from the headmistress, the girlfriend portals the group to a luxury hotel, where staff greet the narrator as the new Silver Fangs guildmaster. The PR manager coaches him to credit Halen training for saving the White Tiger Guild and to defend Nekorians. On a late-night show, the host introduces the paladin as the harem queen's daughter. The narrator mentions his grandfather's place in the first raid beyond level 30 and his parents' deaths in the dungeon before the paladin redirects the host, and she refuses the crew's push for racier behavior.

So far this book: After the first show, Candace calls the group's performance weak and asks to join the coaching. The PR manager moves into Ken's room, and Dez questions her motives; she admits she is drawn to powerful men, and the two agree not to hurt him. A podcast hosted by Carl, a level-10 former adventurer, brings out a surprise guest: Heather, the harem queen, a Halen teacher and Helen's mother, who credits Ken with the final blow against a dwarf queen on the 25th-floor safe zone and teases him about joining her harem.

Afterward an emergency alert sends Ken's portal back to the studio, where dwarf drones are swarming New York. Candace's wind clears the studio and she stays to seal it, while Ken, Dez, Helen, Heather, and the PR manager, followed by a cameraman, track the swarm to Grand Central Station. A dwarven queen on the roof is building a fortress. The party fights her, and Ken disables drones rather than killing them because she raises the dead. Heather's blue fire seems to kill the queen, but she regenerates, and Ken links this to the worms. A larger blast destroys part of the station.

The dwarves keep rampaging, and Ken fears an outbreak among ordinary people. With police and the TACOS adventurer unit holding the line, he uses Eyes of Wisdom to find and kill worm-carrying dwarves. Cameraman Kevin realizes his footage shows what deep divers become. The queen has survived in an office tower; Ken finishes her and her worm using liminal space, a higher stage of his liminal speed. The dwarf bodies do not dissolve into smoke, showing they are not dungeon monsters, and crowds hail Ken as a hero.

So far this book: The UG president questions Ken and Heather. Crimson is being used to screen high-level teams with the detection ability she shares with Ken, and infected people are to be captured and studied, partly so that humans are not seen by the deeper races as an infected species. Brain scans suggest hosts might be recoverable. The president warns Ken away from the demons. The PR manager insists the tour continue, and she, Ken, and Dez begin a relationship; Ken places a magical tattoo on her.

On Gary's talk show Ken learns a viral video calls him the hero of the New York invasion. Dez recounts meeting him in their first year at Halen, where he was the only man admitted. At Gary's after-party, attended with Penny, Charlotte, the whale-race companion, and the cat-race companion, Ken explains that Dez's grimoire turned him, not his own choice. Scanning the room, he finds about a dozen infected adventurers among the staff.

The UG's blue-haired second-in-command asks him to subdue them for study. Gary then unveils Bloodsport, a betting death-match whose fighters are all infected. The party plans for Penny, a frost knight, to freeze hosts while Ken distracts. Dez accepts a challenge and throws her opponent through the kitchen doors. Ken learns that healers revive the losers backstage and suspects revived guests may become infected. He beats the fifth fighter without abilities, breaking his arm, and he and Penny carry the man backstage at the host's invitation.

So far this book: Backstage, Ken and Penny subdue a hallway of worm hosts and send them down to the garage, where the UG director collects them. Ken is uneasy about their likely fate but decides to keep watching the UG's plans. He resolves to hunt hosts across New York, with Penny freezing them, Charlotte keeping captives alive, Dez, the cat-race companion, and the whale-race companion, who can encase people in stone. Separately, Crimson seizes five guests for the UG; two are infected, and the three clean ones are held anyway. A UG healer reports that no ability removes the worm and that a killed host's worm survives a revive.

The party captures ten hosts across the rooftops, then raids a penthouse where a gaunt blonde woman sits in a tub of thousands of worms. She fells two companions with a look and ignores Ken's attacks. He throws everyone through a portal and escapes. Needing a stronger ally, Ken seeks Crimson in Star City, meets the angel Ambrosia, and hears from a succubus that every demon is being checked for worms and that he must report in.

The succubus lord Lady Frey sees he is not a born demon. Ken admits he was human and proves he has no worm. She explains that the Incubus King seized hell after the last shuffle and was killed with most incubi by the other kings, who now seek a new incubus candidate. After hours of negotiation Ken signs her contract: 60 hours of service a year, a share of mana crystals, and a 660 percent repayment rate if she handles the worm threat. She gives him a summoning stone and a vial of her blood for Dez, then tells her princess she has made Ken, 21 and level 52, a demon general.

So far this book: Ken tells his party about the contract and gives Dez the blood vial, and the whale-race companion explains how remarkable his rank as general is. The PR manager reports that the UG president is asking about the people who went missing. Helen, who feels she owes Ken for saving her and her mother, asks to be involved, and he declines. Eyes of Wisdom shows that the powerful host is still in New York and that no one of her strength exists elsewhere on Earth, so Ken summons Lady Frey.

Frey, level 92, arrives, and Crimson joins them, the two sizing each other up. In the penthouse they cut through the hosts; Frey erases one with a pinprick of force. The woman in the tub expected Crimson. Crimson downs three hosts, Frey seizes the woman's movement with telekinesis and breaks her jaw, and the host claims the demons do not grasp the danger to humanity. A pink-haired demon princess arrives, burns the tub of worms, sears the host's gut, offers Ken a steed contract he refuses, and leaves with the prisoner. Crimson concedes the plan worked, and Ken agrees to face the UG with her.

So far this book: The UG president, revealed as a secret summoner whose scars peel away into Valkyries, scolds Ken for bringing a demon into a matter meant to be hidden from other races. Ken refuses to share his deal and the president throws him and Crimson out. Crimson privately admits she was both angry and grateful, gets the group two days of dungeon time, and works Ken through the night in the gravity chamber. Heather sends praise for his clash with the president, and Helen catches a portal ride to Star City for trade.

On floor 53 the party grinds swarms of gale mites; Ken judges they have passed Penny's father and are closing on elite humans. Frey calls through the stone and orders him to kill an incubus rival to the throne. Ken reveals his family are hired assassins. On floor 56 he splits the rival's party with portals, kills the healer, kills a four-armed tank in the tent with liminal space, ignores Frey's late request to take the incubus alive, and kills him with mana implosion, keeping items as proof.

Frey warns that a curse on the dead incubus lets others track the killer for about a week. A five-demon squad led by an imp and sent by a demon prince follows them; Ken's party picks the members off by portal, kills the imp, and captures the other four to hand over to Frey.

So far this book: The tour moves to Chicago and Ken grows more comfortable with interviews. Frey's stone summons him, and he and Dez travel to the third circle of hell, the Imp King's domain. The pink-haired princess introduces herself as Frey's mistress, explains that each king rules a floor, and brings them to a royal gathering at the Sloth Queen's palace, where the elderly Succubus Queen greets them warmly.

At the gathering Ken is tested on which demon groups carry worms and finishes quickly and accurately, seeing through walls. The Succubus Queen has him scan the crowd, and he flags a four-armed Asura prince; the rulers themselves, including the sleeping Sloth Queen, are clean. Suspecting the late Incubus King was infected, which would explain his treaty-breaking, the queen kills the prince despite objections, and a worm is pulled from his body. Dozens more are killed and inspected, with the clean to be revived and compensated. She calls Ken her future Incubus King and warns he has made many enemies.

The princess, who plans someday to take the Succubus Queen's seat, takes over selling his scanning services. Ken spends hours finding hosts in a succubus lady's city and watches the royals erase them without any interest in saving them, which disturbs him. Dez receives a research tome to help improve herself. When Ken asks the UG president for the cure research, the president refuses, saying his place in the demon hierarchy makes him untrustworthy.

So far this book: Weeks of interviews pass as the tour heads toward Texas and then Europe; Ken is called to hell for scans only twice, and the UG shares nothing more. The PR manager is training her body and combat skills and doing side work for Crimson. On the way to a lunch, a group of non-humans with the strength of worm hosts attacks; their orc-like leader, speaking for the parasites, demands Ken's sight and threatens to take everyone he loves. The pink-haired princess appears, pins them, and carries off the leader, having expected retaliation after the palace purge. Ken confirms everyone is safe and tells the PR manager he and the UG are no longer on good terms.

The class trains for weeks on floor 58, where its trial monster is the red-lightning hawk that gave Crimson her limit break. Ken decides to keep his schedule predictable as bait so the parasites target him. Helen's party arrives seeking a different reward, and Heather throws students at the hawk.

Scanning his class, Ken finds an infected classmate, the daughter of a UG director. The president ignores him, and the director turns out to be shut out of the parasite data herself; Ken does not tell her it is her daughter. The party decides to act without the UG. Crimson is refused entry at the UG facility but leaves three body bags holding Ken, Charlotte, and Penny in masks made by his grandmother. Inside, an exhausted doctor tends them while taking orders from a smoky-voiced figure who calls hosts siblings.

So far this book: The doctor is not infected; the parasites seized the facility when Crimson stopped her deliveries, and all new patients, including her earlier drop-offs, are now hosts. He believes he is close to a cure and explains that the worms strip away a host's natural limits, making them far stronger but wearing them out within weeks. Crimson warns him never to make it into an enhancement drug. Crimson, the cat-race companion, the PR manager, and Dez join through a portal, and the party brings him test subjects. Removing a worm kills the host beyond revival, so he tries laser extraction under sedation. Crimson decides to wipe out the Earth nest, and the party freezes six hosts in the facility freezer, where worms go dormant.

Near the dungeon entrance, captives are being forced to level, and Ken and Crimson kill most of a dozen hosts, planning revives later. A huge orc-like host with an axe says Ken killed his relative, the bathtub breeder, and badly wounds him and Penny. Worms pour from the floor ponds and merge with him into a giant mass. The cat-race companion brings word that a sedated patient exploded and the doctor is dead.

Worms strike Dez, who burns them away. Ken lures the mass by portal into the freezer, where the cold slows it and the party smashes it apart. The lab is ruined, but the doctor's first patient lived. At the cat-race companion's suggestion, Ken builds liminal stacks in the dungeon, enters liminal time, cuts the worm out of his infected classmate, and crushes it. A sedative calms her, and she survives. Heather then arrives and looks at Ken.

characters.description: The narrator, a former human who now carries demonic traits. He can spot Threadspawn hosts and opens portals at will. He has just removed a worm from his classmate Selene by surgery and raided a UG research lab that the worms had overrun, so the UG is now hostile to him. He intends to pass what he learned to the elves, the demons and the Orkai, and he is advised to gather enough allies that the UG has to deal with him as an equal.
characters.name: Ken

characters.description: Ken's mentor and the most dangerous human on his side. The UG is afraid of her, and simply having her nearby keeps Ken safe from its reprisals while the fallout from the lab raid and Selene's surgery settles.
characters.name: Crimson

characters.description: A calm, experienced senior adventurer known by the title of Harem Queen. She accepts Ken's account of Selene's infection because he and Crimson can detect hosts. She supports him while scolding him, tells him to confess to the UG director and to warn her before operating on any classmate again, and stays at Halen to watch the class for further infections.
characters.name: Heather

characters.description: A Halen classmate and the daughter of a UG director. She was a Threadspawn host, and Ken has just cut the worm out of her. She lies unconscious and sedated while Charlotte watches over her.
characters.name: Selene

characters.description: A member of Ken's party and its healer. After the surgery she tends Selene and keeps watch over her recovery, then helps move her somewhere safer.
characters.name: Charlotte

characters.description: One of Ken's partners and a member of his party. She is quick to tease him, including about the cat-person companion acting as a nurse after Selene's surgery.
characters.name: Dez

characters.description: A member of Ken's party who stands by him as the consequences of Selene's surgery and the UG lab raid begin to land.
characters.name: Penny

characters.description: A cat-person in Ken's household and party. After Selene's surgery she acts as a nurse, helping Charlotte care for the sedated girl and take her away to recover.
characters.name: Cat-person companion

characters.description: A senior UG official and Selene's mother. Heather tells Ken he must confess to her what he did to her daughter. Her husband is said to be unstable and dangerous.
characters.name: UG director

characters.description: A media figure Ken trusts. He plans to get in touch with her as soon as he leaves Halen after Selene's surgery.
characters.name: Belair

characters.description: Selene's father and the UG director's husband. He was released from prison only recently, after serving time for mass murder, and is known for violence. He comes with his wife when she confronts Ken about their daughter.
characters.name: Selene's father

characters.description: A tall, heavily built succubus in the demon hierarchy to which Ken belongs. She calls him her favorite former human, prizes his eyes, and reminds him that he still owes her favors. She treats his worm-removal method as something to trade with demon royals, insists on a trade rather than a favor, promises him protection within her hierarchy, and says a hell embassy will soon open in Star City.
characters.name: Lady Frey

characters.description: An elderly Orkai arbiter who walks with a cane yet remains strong, and who has crossed paths with Ken before. He reads whether people are telling the truth, confirms that nobody lied about Selene's cure, and takes her into Orkai care. He warns that reporting a host to the Orkai currently amounts to a death sentence for that host.
characters.name: Orkai judge-arbiter

characters.description: Ken's grandfather, an eager fighter with several wives. He greets Ken with a surprise sword attack, insists that a Nagato does not run, and pushes for a direct confrontation with the UG.
characters.name: Ken's grandfather

characters.description: Wives of Ken's grandfather. Two of them appear first: a gentle one who bakes, and a sharp strategist who can rein in the grandfather and advises an indirect approach to the UG. Ken's late mother was the daughter of one of the grandmothers.
characters.name: Ken's grandmothers

characters.description: The scarred and nervous head of the UG. When his board investors brush off Crimson and Ken's media attack and propose a smear campaign, he is the only one who warns that Crimson could kill them. Crimson's nickname for him is scaredy cat.
characters.name: UG president

characters.description: Ruler of the elves and Ken's wife, with ruby hair and sun-kissed skin. She wants more of his time and is tired of her nobles. Ken gives her a serum vial and explains the extraction method. A drow assassin then attacks her in her bedroom, and Ken stops him.
characters.name: Elf empress

characters.description: A silver-haired elven royal censor who has completed her trial and fights with red limit-break lightning. She knocks out a heckling noble, wants a portal to Earth so she can fight Crimson, and throws the drow assassin out of the window before chasing him.
characters.name: Silver-haired royal censor

characters.description: The empress's partner, an armored guard who is now a royal censor. She was once the tank in Ken's party until Penny took that role, and she is one of Ken's lovers. She turns down his offer to rejoin because her people need her.
characters.name: Empress's partner censor

characters.description: A grey-skinned drow killer who coats his blade with an oily poison. He gets into the elven palace and attacks the empress in her bedroom, but Ken blocks him and the silver-haired censor drives him out.
characters.name: Drow assassin

characters.description: An elven royal censor whom the silver-haired censor assigns to guard the empress after the assassination attempt.
characters.name: Younger royal censor

characters.description: A female drow armed with curved daggers. She squares off against Ken during the fight at the twentieth-floor safe zone where the drow hold Naga as forced laborers.
characters.name: Drow dagger fighter

characters.description: A powerful female drow who comes down on a thread to take over a fight in a dungeon safe zone. The other drow kneel to her. She claims the territory for her people, kicks the silver-haired censor away with ease, and tells Ken that alliances with elves mean nothing given what waits deeper in the dungeon.
characters.name: Strong drow leader

characters.description: A wealthy UG board member whom Ken and his grandfather track to an estate in France. They overhear her hiring adventurers to kill Crimson, including a discussion of poisoning her with radiation.
characters.name: Board member at the French estate

characters.description: A UG board member known for double-crossing deals. Dez and one of Ken's grandmothers attack him in his high-rise, and he dies from his own grenade.
characters.name: Board member in the high-rise

characters.description: An eager Halen classmate who answers the questions in Crimson's lesson on poisons.
characters.name: Candace

characters.description: A Halen classmate who backs giving extra exercise to a troublesome former party support in Crimson's training.
characters.name: Helen

characters.description: A creature that travels with Ken's group. During the raid on a drow settlement it chews through the drow webs to keep Charlotte safe.
characters.name: Bun-Bun

characters.description: A worm living in a dying human woman held as a drow slave. Unlike any Threadspawn Ken has met before, it is afraid and begs to be spared. It says it was bred in a drow pool and placed into broken workers to keep them laboring, and that drow venom prevents it from taking drow hosts. Ken has it removed, and Charlotte heals the woman.
characters.name: Frightened Threadspawn

characters.description: A small, pink-haired succubus who outranks Lady Frey by a wide margin and moves extremely fast. She and Frey want Ken to find and remove Threadspawn among the demons, and she carries him to hell to start the work.
characters.name: Demon princess

characters.description: A large shade who leads the shades, the tank caste among the demons, and holds infected shades in a cell in hell. Ken is told to treat an uninfected shade first, and while he pretends to cure that one he removes a worm from the shade beside it. The prince then uses the staged cure to clear the uninfected shade of past crimes.
characters.name: Shade prince

characters.description: The ruler of the succubi, grey-haired and grandmotherly in appearance, regarded by demons as close to a god. Her skin turns Ken's blades aside. She has been watching his fights with the drow, says she has stood before the gates at the very bottom of the dungeon, promises the Threadspawn will be wiped out, and urges Ken to stop fighting like a human and draw on his demon side.
characters.name: Succubus Queen

characters.description: An assassin-type drow from a scouting party that ambushes Ken and Penny. Ken brings her under Greater Charm, and she and the other charmed drow turn on the rest of their group and then serve him as he prepares to attack their fortress.
characters.name: Charmed drow servant

characters.description: A strong drow officer who defends the fortress during Ken's assault. Heather's Absolute Reflect has no effect on her, and after Ken wounds her with Mana Implosion she crushes his chest. Heather, Crimson and Ken then kill her. As she dies she swears to hunt down Ken and his women and to infect him with a worm.
characters.name: Drow lieutenant

characters.description: An older cat-person woman who raised the cat-person companion. She is found among cat-person captives in a drow-held safe zone, is wary of Ken at first, and organizes her people for the evacuation.
characters.name: Cat-person foster mother

characters.description: A self-assured young woman who recognizes Ken at a mall escape room during his date with Selene. With three friends she pushes into the date and films the pair on their phones, and the encounter ends with Selene lifting her off her feet in a confrontation.
characters.name: Mall fan leader

characters.description: A spoiled young heiress to the estate of a dead UG board member. Under pressure she admits to allying with the Threadspawn, planning to arm her security force with them, and handing them full access to UG information. Ken wounds her with a venom-coated dagger, charms her and takes her CID.
characters.name: Bank heiress

characters.description: An elf at the Nagato breakfast table. She calculates how Ken's new incubation skill works, connects elf-human marriage to political stakes, and points out that controlling the UG effectively makes Ken a human king.
characters.name: Elf princess

recaps.ending: The book closes at the Nagato estate. Ken is level 58, a demon general under Lady Frey, and part of the group that holds a majority stake in the UG, which also makes him the target of a lawsuit from the old board's heirs. Using Stat Incubation on Selene has temporarily cost him 58 strength. Selene now has a heart-shaped mark and considers herself part of his harem. Crimson is level 78, alive, and will coach Penny, whose limit break is still hard to control. Charlotte, alive again after being revived, is preparing for a trial boss that tests mana endurance and is training with Ken's grandfather. Dez is researching a ritual to turn herself into a full succubus, with a grandmother helping and Ken as the medium. The cat-person companion has freed her people, but she grieves what it cost them while they settle near a dungeon on national parkland. Open questions remain about the UG: the UG president is still in office, and the UG director wants his job, though Ken does not trust her. Threadspawn hosts are loose on Earth again, and the bank heiress has given them UG data. The level 92 drow leader is still alive, other drow fortresses stand, and the drow intend to enslave the sun elves. Ken still owes the demon hierarchy, the incubus king path is open, and he remains uneasy about Final Fascination. Helen's feelings for him have not been addressed. The book's last move is Ken challenging Crimson to a race to the bottom of the dungeon.
recaps.in_short: After Ken cuts a Threadspawn worm out of his classmate Selene and raids a UG lab, the UG turns on him. Crimson and the media figure Belair answer with a public exposé, and Selene recovers under Orkai care. At the elven palace Ken finds worm hosts and foils a drow attempt on the empress's life, which pulls his party into a war with slaving drow deep in the dungeon. Ken, his party and his grandparents kill all six UG board members and collect enough stock plates for the group to control the UG. Serving the demons as a worm remover, he meets the Succubus Queen, reaches level 58, and learns that the Threadspawn may have been bred by the drow. A raid on a drow fortress leaves Charlotte and Ken dead for a time. Both are revived, the fortress falls, and its slaves are freed. The cat-person companion's tribe of about 2,000 is then evacuated to Nebraska. The old board's heirs sue Ken and try to smear him, and the trail reveals that their heiress has allied with the Threadspawn. Ken brings Selene into his harem and ends the book planning a leveling push and a race with Crimson to the bottom of the dungeon.

recaps.text: Previously: Ken was once human but became an incubus, and he now serves the demon hierarchy while attending a dungeon college class taught by Crimson, the fiercest adventurer on his side. He belongs to the Nagato family, leads the Silver Fangs guild, and lives with a household of partners: Dez, Penny, Charlotte and a cat-person companion. A creature called Bun-Bun travels with the group, and a black-winged angel is also part of the household. Ken is married to the elf empress. His most important ability is Eyes of Wisdom, which shows him hidden things, including Threadspawn, the parasitic worms that take control of their hosts. Ken has dealings with the Orkai and their arbiters, and the demons hold debts over him. Threads carried into this book include Crimson's debt to the arbiters, Charlotte's wedding plans, and the war between the elves and the Naga.

So far this book: Ken has cut a Threadspawn worm out of his classmate Selene, daughter of a UG director, after his party raided a UG research lab that the worms had taken over. Heather, the Harem Queen, accepts what he did but tells him to confess to the director and warns that the UG will be furious. In Star City, Lady Frey treats the extraction as a trade good for demon royals. The old Orkai judge-arbiter confirms that Selene is clean and moves her into Orkai care, and the director, arriving with her violent husband, agrees to hold off on punishing Ken while her daughter recovers. At the Nagato estate Ken's grandfather wants an open fight, while a grandmother advises a less direct route. Crimson arrives and reports that she has told the heads of the five major dungeon colleges that the UG blocked a cure for an infected student. Ken brings in Belair, who runs a media campaign. At the wrecked lab, Crimson, Belair and Ken film an exposé: the UG had Crimson bring suspects there, some were infected, and doctors refuse to share anything. Belair promises to publish quickly, and Crimson declares war on the UG. In a bunker, the UG president warns his six board investors that Crimson could kill them, but they plan to smear her and Ken instead.

So far this book: Belair's exposé goes viral and the public sides with Crimson. Ken travels to the elf world, gives his wife the empress a serum vial and explains the extraction, and tells the elves he has joined the demon hierarchy. His Eyes of Wisdom find five elf hosts in the palace, and they are petrified and jailed. That night a drow assassin attacks the empress. Ken blocks him and a silver-haired royal censor drives him off, then brings him back captured. The censor, who turns out to be the empress's great-aunt and Crimson's longtime rival, follows a trail into the dungeon with Ken. On the twentieth floor they find drow forcing shackled Naga to work. A fight escalates until a powerful drow leader arrives, overwhelms the censor, and tells Ken that elf alliances are worthless given what lies deeper. Ken calls for help, and Crimson comes through a portal with the rest of the party. Crimson and the censor take on the drow leader, whom Ken reads at level 92 against Crimson's 79, while the party defeats the other drow and the Naga. Crimson drives the leader away, and both fighters are badly hurt. Back at the palace, one of Ken's grandmothers, a specialist in torture, begins questioning the captured assassin.

So far this book: The silver-haired censor challenges Crimson to a duel and loses badly. Eyes of Wisdom show Ken a route toward the cat-person companion's lost people. In the Orkai hospital, the UG director says Selene will recover. She explains that the UG belongs to the heirs of its founding families, who skim profits and have never dived, and she urges Ken to kill them while sparing the president. Her husband quietly gives Ken a list of the board members' estates. With Crimson scouting the dungeon, each party member pairs with one of Ken's grandparents. Ken and his grandfather catch one board member in France hiring killers to go after Crimson, kill the hired adventurers and then kill her. Dez and a grandmother kill another in his high-rise. By the end all six board members are dead. The president calls to apologize, and Ken pretends to know nothing. From the dead members, the group gathers 55 UG stock plates, a majority, split into 11 each among Ken, Dez, Charlotte, Penny and Crimson. Crimson, who is privately devoted to Ken, accepts her share. She reports that the cat-people lie beyond drow lines and that some Naga captives of the drow carry Threadspawn, so the two goals become one. The party trains and fights small drow raids, and Selene wakes up.

So far this book: The Orkai copy Ken's serum and prepare to remove worms from four hosts, and they give him a dossier on the drow. Selene returns to class, and Crimson makes Ken her tutor. At her home Selene tries to seduce him. Her berserker father chases him off until her mother orders her husband to stop. A large raid with two elven censors breaks a drow web settlement. Among its slaves the cat-person companion finds a warrior from her tribe, and Ken finds a frightened worm in a dying woman.
